[MUQATIL:47:16/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The people listening to Muhammad here are hypocrites.
[MUQATIL:47:16/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Among the listeners were Rifaah ibn Zayd, al-Harith ibn Amr, and an ally of Banu Zuhra; after Muhammad criticized hypocrites in his Friday sermon, they kept quiet and left.
[MUQATIL:47:16/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Those given knowledge are guided by the Quran; Muqatil identifies them here as Abdullah ibn Masud al-Hudhali.
[MUQATIL:47:16/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The hypocrites ask what Muhammad just said despite having heard him, because they did not understand his words.
[MUQATIL:47:16/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God sealed their hearts with disbelief so they cannot understand faith, and they follow their desires in disbelief.
[FARRA:v3p60/r1] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | They listen to the Prophet's Friday sermon without understanding; after leaving with the people they mockingly ask the Muslims what he just said, and God describes their sealed hearts.
[MAJAZ:v2p215/r2] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | Min here functions as a plural expression.

[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r2] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · أبو زيد | reports | Abu Zayd explains ائتنفت الكلام as beginning speech anew, the sense intended by the verse's آنفا.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r3] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · السكري | reports | Al-Sukkari says الأنف in poetry means people who refuse humiliation; al-Farisi says those examples do not bear the verse's sense of beginning.

[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p192/r5] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · author | holds | A poem uses الأنف as a resolute adjective; a Sibawayh line about نمر illustrates a parallel broken plural pattern.

[THALABI:v9p32#2/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says of those given knowledge: I am among them, and I was among those asked.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Mawardi identifies the listeners as hypocrites: Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Rifa'a ibn al-Tabut, Zayd ibn al-Sulayt, al-Harith ibn Amr, and Malik ibn al-Dakhsham.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r10] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Anif can mean recently or at the beginning.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r11] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Their question may mock what they heard or seek information about what they failed to understand.

[MAWARDI-FULL:v5p297/r9] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | This is the hypocrites' question to the knowledgeable people after leaving the Prophet.

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas said, as transmitted by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he himself was among those whom the hypocrites questioned.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · عطاء عن ابن عباس وابن بريدة ومقاتل | reports | Ata's report from Ibn Abbas identifies the knowledgeable person as Abdullah ibn Masud; Ibn Burayda and Muqatil hold the same view.

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | rejects | A report through al-Bazzi attributes to Ibn Kathir the form أنفا بالقمر, but al-Wahidi treats it as a mistaken supposition and upholds the common reading.

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p238/r9] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الزجاج | prefers | Al-Zajjaj prefers that the hypocrites asked mockingly to show that they had not listened or paid attention; the alternative is that they heard but did not understand.
